narratives.name: Application Platform Domain Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Application Platform Domain alpha matters within the TDP framework.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers face compounding application platform challenges -- legacy application portfolios limiting agility, developer teams slowed by manual operations and inconsistent environments, and increasing regulatory pressure on software supply chain security. Without a structured positioning approach, sellers struggle to identify which of these concerns is the customer's primary driver and how to connect technology capabilities to business outcomes.

The Application Platform Domain structures seller engagement around a progressive assessment-to-decision journey. Starting with application landscape characterization, sellers identify which of three tactics matches the customer's primary challenge, then execute structured conversations with domain-specific credentials, customer proof, and competitive positioning. Technical validation demonstrates platform capabilities against the customer's specific requirements.

Structured application platform positioning enables sellers to engage credibly across diverse developer and platform engineering scenarios, from legacy modernization to internal developer platform creation to supply chain security. Win attribution tracks domain effectiveness and enables continuous content optimization.

citationNames: Sales Plays, TDPs and Sales Tactics

narratives.name: App Platform TDP Practice Intent
narratives.description: The end-to-end narrative of how the Application Platform TDP progresses from landscape assessment through tactic execution to platform decision.

narrativeContexts.context: Enterprise customers face a convergence of application platform challenges -- modernizing legacy applications while building cloud-native capabilities, creating productive developer experiences without sacrificing governance, and securing the software supply chain from source to deployment. The Application Platform TDP addresses these through three focused tactics that equip sellers to engage credibly across these distinct but related technology decisions.

The practice's value is validated through its alignment of Red Hat OpenShift's platform capabilities to three measurable customer outcomes: accelerated application delivery through modernization, improved developer productivity through platform engineering, and reduced supply chain risk through trusted build pipelines. Each tactic provides structured What to Say/Share/Show content tailored to both business and technical decision makers.

Sellers activate the Application Platform TDP by assessing customer application landscapes, identifying which tactic matches the customer's primary challenge, and executing structured conversations with audience-appropriate evidence. Technical validation demonstrates developer onboarding, application modernization approaches, and supply chain security features.

Active field engagement reveals which tactic-customer combinations drive highest conversion, enabling targeted content refinement and competitive positioning updates against cloud PaaS alternatives and competing container platforms.

Performance data validates tactic effectiveness and informs content optimization. Developer experience demonstrations and platform engineering proof-of-value results feed back into the evidence base. Win stories strengthen positioning for subsequent engagements.

Mature Application Platform TDP execution expands through cross-TDP solution narratives connecting to AI Platform, Automation, and Server/Cloud OS, creating integrated platform stories for complex enterprise engagements.

narratives.name: Optimize Traditional Apps Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Optimize Traditional Apps tactic matters for application platform positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Organizations with large portfolios of traditional applications on legacy platforms face mounting operational costs, limited agility, and growing security exposure. Development teams spend excessive time on infrastructure concerns rather than business features, and modernization initiatives stall due to perceived risk and complexity.

The Optimize Traditional Apps tactic equips sellers to frame the modernization challenge from the customer's perspective, presenting Red Hat OpenShift as the platform that reduces modernization risk through assessment tooling, migration utilities, and proven approaches ranging from lift-and-shift to refactoring.

Sellers who use this tactic establish credibility by demonstrating understanding of the customer's modernization barriers before positioning solutions, converting more effectively than product-led approaches.

narratives.name: Secure Software Supply Chain Tactic Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why the Secure Software Supply Chain tactic matters for application platform positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Software supply chain attacks have escalated from theoretical risk to board-level concern. Organizations face increasing regulatory requirements for software composition transparency, vulnerability management, and provenance attestation. Most development pipelines lack visibility into the dependencies and components flowing through build processes.

The Secure Software Supply Chain tactic equips sellers to frame supply chain security as both a risk management imperative and a regulatory compliance enabler, presenting Red Hat's trusted content, certified images, and integrated pipeline security as the foundation for a verifiable software supply chain.

Sellers using this tactic establish urgency through industry incident data and regulatory requirements, then demonstrate Red Hat's unique position as both the platform provider and the trusted content source, converting through demonstrable compliance alignment and pipeline security proof.

narratives.name: Application Platform Competitive Position Context and Rationale
narratives.description: Why multi-level competitive intelligence is essential for application platform positioning.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform evaluations involve a diverse competitive landscape spanning cloud-native PaaS offerings, alternative container platforms, and internal platform builds. Each competitor category requires distinct positioning approaches -- cloud PaaS competitors emphasize convenience and integration, container alternatives emphasize simplicity, and internal builds emphasize customization.

Cloud providers offer deeply integrated PaaS solutions (AWS EKS/ECS, Azure AKS, Google GKE) with strong cloud-specific tooling. Alternative container platforms (Rancher, Tanzu) offer simplified management for specific deployment models. Internal developer platform builds offer maximum customization but require significant platform team investment.

Red Hat's application platform advantage lies at the intersection of enterprise readiness, multi-cloud portability, integrated security (including trusted software supply chain), and developer experience. The platform provides the foundation for internal developer platforms with golden paths and governance built in, avoiding cloud lock-in while delivering enterprise-grade operations across any infrastructure.

The App Platform Positioning Brief provides progressive depth from market overview through credentialed positioning to complete engagement content, organizing application platform-specific credentials, customer proof, and competitive positioning by audience type and tactic scenario.

Sellers using the fully developed positioning brief can engage credibly in any of the three application platform tactic conversations with appropriate credentials, evidence, and competitive differentiation.

narratives.name: Assess Application Platform Landscape Guidance
narratives.description: How to conduct effective application platform landscape assessment for tactic selection.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform evaluations involve diverse customer scenarios -- some organizations need to modernize legacy monoliths, others need to build internal developer platforms, and others face supply chain security mandates. Without structured assessment, sellers may position the wrong tactic or miss the customer's primary concern entirely.

The assessment evaluates the customer's application portfolio composition, development practice maturity, and supply chain security posture to identify which of the three application platform tactics best matches their primary challenge.

A focused assessment produces clear tactic selection, enabling the seller to engage with the most relevant challenge framing, evidence, and demonstration content rather than attempting to cover all three scenarios in a single engagement.

narratives.name: Define Application Platform Strategy Guidance
narratives.description: How to collaborate with customer stakeholders on application platform strategy definition.

narrativeContexts.context: Without a defined platform strategy, application modernization initiatives lack direction and developer experience improvements lack architectural foundation. Customers need structured guidance to translate their assessment findings into an actionable platform approach.

Platform strategy definition works with customer stakeholders to outline the IDP architecture, prioritize modernization candidates by approach, define supply chain security requirements, and establish productivity baselines. The strategy connects assessment findings to Red Hat OpenShift's specific capabilities.

A defined platform strategy provides the foundation for tactic-level engagement, enabling the seller to demonstrate specific capabilities against the customer's agreed-upon approach rather than generic platform features.

narratives.name: Execute App Platform Tactic Conversation Guidance
narratives.description: How to deliver challenge-focused application platform tactic conversations effectively.

narrativeContexts.context: Product-led application platform pitches fail because they position features before establishing the customer's specific challenge. Developers and platform engineers respond to solutions that address their daily pain, not to product capability overviews.

Each tactic conversation opens with customer challenge framing, uses audience-segmented messaging and evidence, and includes demonstrations directly relevant to the specific challenge. The seller navigates between tactic content and Application Platform TDP credentials seamlessly.

Challenge-first tactic conversations convert more effectively because they establish relevance and urgency before positioning platform capabilities, enabling deeper customer engagement and clearer qualification.

narratives.name: Position App Platform Competitively Guidance
narratives.description: How to build and deploy competitive positioning in application platform evaluations.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform competitive landscapes vary by customer context -- some evaluate Red Hat against cloud-native PaaS, others against alternative container platforms, and others against internal platform builds. Each scenario requires distinct competitive positioning approaches.

Cloud PaaS offerings provide deep cloud-specific integration and managed convenience. Alternative container platforms offer simplified management for specific deployment models. Internal builds offer maximum customization at the cost of significant platform team investment.

Red Hat's application platform advantage combines enterprise-grade operations with multi-cloud portability, integrated developer experience with governance, and trusted software supply chain with platform-integrated security -- addressing the gaps in each competitive alternative.

narratives.name: Validate App Platform Technology Fit Guidance
narratives.description: How to structure and execute technical validation for application platform scenarios.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform evaluations require proof that goes beyond feature demonstrations. Customers need to see developer onboarding improvements, modernization feasibility for their specific applications, and supply chain security integration with their existing toolchains.

Technical validation is structured around the specific tactic scenario -- developer onboarding and golden path execution for DevX, migration assessment and containerization for Optimize Apps, or pipeline security and SBOM generation for Supply Chain. Success criteria are aligned to the customer's business outcomes.

Structured technical validation produces documented results that the customer champion can use to justify the platform decision internally, accelerating procurement cycles and strengthening deal commitment.

narratives.name: Build App Platform TDP Content Guidance
narratives.description: How to systematically build application platform TDP content across three tactic scenarios.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform sellers need comprehensive positioning materials covering three distinct tactic scenarios, each with its own competitive landscape, customer proof requirements, and technical demonstration needs. Ad hoc content creation leads to inconsistent positioning.

TDP content building follows the systematic approach from the parent practice -- domain definition, credential assembly, customer win documentation, audience-segmented messaging, and demonstration preparation -- applied to each of the three application platform tactic scenarios.
Complete application platform TDP content enables any seller to engage credibly across all three tactic scenarios with appropriate credentials, evidence, and competitive differentiation.

narratives.name: Optimize App Platform TDP Performance Guidance
narratives.description: How to continuously refine application platform TDP content based on performance data.

narrativeContexts.context: Application platform positioning that is not continuously refined loses effectiveness as cloud providers announce new capabilities, developer tooling evolves, and supply chain security standards mature. Static tactic content fails to reflect current competitive realities.

Optimization examines per-tactic conversion data, competitive win/loss patterns, and field feedback to identify specific improvements. Underperforming tactics are redesigned, competitive positioning is refreshed with latest analyst evaluations, and new customer wins are added to evidence bases.

Continuous optimization sustains application platform TDP effectiveness across market cycles, ensuring that credentials, competitive positioning, and tactic content reflect current technology landscape and customer expectations.

patterns.name: App Platform Technical Engagement Journey
patterns.description: Pattern coordinating how an application platform TDP engagement progresses from landscape assessment through tactic execution to platform decision.

patternViews.name: Prerequisites
patternViews.description: Sales Play engagement has identified Application Platform as relevant.

narrativeContexts.context: The application platform engagement journey begins when a Sales Play engagement identifies application modernization, developer experience, or software supply chain security as areas requiring technology-specific depth and TDP-level positioning.

patternViews.name: Assessment
patternViews.description: Customer application landscape evaluated and tactic identified.

narrativeContexts.context: Assessment evaluates the customer's application portfolio, development practices, and supply chain maturity to identify which of the three application platform tactics best matches their primary challenge. Competitive landscape is mapped to prepare for technology-specific positioning.

patternViews.name: Positioning and Credentialing
patternViews.description: Application platform credentials established and platform strategy defined.

narrativeContexts.context: Red Hat's application platform credentials are established through seller credentials, analyst recognition, and customer success stories. The platform strategy is defined collaboratively with the customer, connecting their specific challenges to OpenShift's capabilities across modernization, developer experience, and supply chain security.

patternViews.name: Tactic Execution
patternViews.description: Customer engaged with challenge-focused conversations and competitive positioning deployed.

narrativeContexts.context: Tactic execution delivers customer challenge-focused conversations with audience-segmented content. Competitive positioning is deployed against cloud PaaS alternatives and competing container platforms. Cross-TDP navigation to Automation or Container Management is established when the customer's needs span technology domains.

patternViews.name: Validation and Decision
patternViews.description: Application platform capabilities validated and platform decision secured.

narrativeContexts.context: Technical validation demonstrates application platform capabilities against the customer's specific requirements -- developer onboarding improvements, modernization feasibility, or supply chain security compliance. Results are documented for the customer's internal decision process.

Post-decision, the engagement expands through adoption roadmap execution, expansion to additional teams and applications, and cross-TDP solution narratives connecting application platform to AI infrastructure, automation, and infrastructure modernization for broader organizational impact.
